Recommendation: Once FIDO2 is enabled (see AUTH004), require attestation so only certified, known security key models can be registered. Two documented side effects to plan for, both from Microsoft's own docs. First, enforcing attestation suppresses the registration campaign nudge entirely for affected users (see RCAMP001) - the campaign will appear enabled and simply reach nobody. Second, synced passkeys do not support attestation at all, so enforcing it also blocks every synced provider regardless of what PASS003 reports. Also worth knowing: attestation is evaluated only at registration time, so turning it on later does not retroactively invalidate passkeys already registered without it - existing weaker registrations need finding and cleaning up separately. Side effect worth knowing about: Microsoft's documented Bluetooth-based cross-device fallback for registering a 'Passkey in Microsoft Authenticator' from a different device than the phone it will live on is explicitly unavailable whenever attestation is enforced. That fallback matters specifically when a new user's Temporary Access Pass is one-time-use and was already consumed reaching Security Info on a laptop, leaving the phone-side registration step with no other way to authenticate (see TAP001 and the New User Bootstrap flow for the full trace). Not a reason to leave attestation off - just something to plan around (a short-lived multi-use TAP for onboarding, or Windows Hello for Business as the same-device alternative).
